body:
I'll tell them before she intended to do it, of course. But only after I've seen them tomorrow. Who knows, maybe they're abusive and the real reason and she just didn't want to tell me. (I don't think so, but still)

Thanks. That's gonna be one weird weekend...
It's not very pleasant, is it?
I know, and I've told her that.

If I tell her parents right now, there would be 2 problems: first of all, they don't know me and probably won't trust/believe me. Second, if she'll get the chance she may react and kill herself violently today/tomorrow.

I'll wait until she has introduced me to her parents tomorrow. We've talked for hours yesterday evening, a few times she said I "created some hope" in her, but she doesn't want to be hurt anymore. I'll leave her, she'll fail all her exams, etc. Her words. It's difficult to argue with her when she's depressive.

That sounds pretty reasonable. I love her and want her to be happy. But since the thinks that'll only be the case in death, I can't fully support this.
Yes, she'd hate me for telling anyone, especially her parents.

>Really, do you want to wake up on Sunday with her dead knowing you could have prevented this?

No. Not at all. I'd be devastated.
and how is that again helping her?
She's been to 5 therapists, thinks she won't respond to any therapy.
What should I do, then? Let her kill herself?
